note: Frames taken from the shots photographers and photo guides repeat at each stop, set to the hour you are there. Open one for where to stand, the light, and how. Person means someone from your group is the subject.

shots.stand: In front of the gate, on the center line, looking through it down Nakamise.
shots.angle: Stand outside the gate, centered on the lantern. The lantern hangs in the top half. Nakamise runs through the opening to Hozomon.
shots.light: 07:00. The lantern is still lit and the street through the gate is empty. This is the frame that is gone by 08:00.
how: Hold the camera at eye level.
Keep the lantern and the far gate in one frame.
One frame, then step inside.

shots.stand: Inside the gate, full length, the lantern overhead.
shots.angle: Inside Kaminarimon. One person from your group is full length under the lantern. The posts sit at the edges.
shots.light: 07:00. Expose for their face. The lantern stays bright.
how: They look up at the lantern.
You stay inside the gate.
One frame, then clear the opening.

shots.stand: On Nakamise, full length, Hozomon and the pagoda behind them.
shots.angle: A few shops up Nakamise. One person, full length, walking toward you. Hozomon is centered behind them. The pagoda can sit above the roofs to one side.
shots.light: Morning, stalls still shut, so the eaves are clean lines.
how: They walk. They look ahead.
You step aside so you are not in the middle of the street.
One frame.

shots.stand: Crouch at the censer and shoot through the smoke at the hall.
shots.angle: At the incense burner, camera near the smoke. The hall roof fills the top. The smoke is the layer between you and the hall.
shots.light: 07:40, once the incense is going. Expose for the wood.
how: Crouch. Do not stand in the worship line.
One frame when the smoke crosses the hall.
Photos inside the main hall are not allowed.

shots.stand: Middle of the street, the kappa sign overhead, the street going back.
shots.angle: Stand in the middle of Kappabashi. The kappa sign is at the top. The street and the shop signs recede under it.
shots.light: Late morning. The sign is brighter than the street. Expose for the sign.
how: Include the sign and enough street to show where you are.
One frame when the road under the sign is clear.
Then move to the sidewalk.

shots.stand: At a sample-food window, one dish filling the frame.
shots.angle: At Ganso or a shop window. One plastic dish fills the frame. The rest of the window is the edge.
shots.light: The shop light on the food. Step until the glass reflection of the street is out of the dish.
how: Pick one dish, not the whole window.
Focus on the food.
One frame.

shots.stand: In the lane, the train girders as the ceiling, stalls on both sides.
shots.angle: Stand in the market lane under the tracks. The girders fill the top. Stalls line both sides and the lane goes back.
shots.light: Midday comes through in patches. Shoot where a stall light is warmer than the street.
how: Eye level, down the lane.
Wait for a gap in the middle.
One frame.

shots.stand: One counter, the goods stacked, filling the frame.
shots.angle: At one stall. The counter and the stacked goods fill the frame. The seller's hands can be in it if they are working.
shots.light: The stall bulb. Let the street behind go dark.
how: Step in close so the stall is the whole picture.
Ask with a nod if you are across the counter from the seller.
One frame.

shots.stand: From the causeway, the hall on the island, water in the lower half.
shots.angle: From the causeway or the east shore of Shinobazu. The Benten hall sits on the island. Water fills the lower half. The roof is complete.
shots.light: Early afternoon. Keep the horizon level. Expose for the hall.
how: A person walking the causeway can stay small at the edge.
The hall is the subject.
One frame, then leave for Gyoen. Last entry there is 16:00.

shots.stand: On the lawn, the greenhouse centered, sky only a strip.
shots.angle: From the lawn in front of the greenhouse. The building is centered. The grass fills the lower half. The sky is a strip at the top.
shots.light: Afternoon, before last entry at 16:00. Side light if the sky is clear. Expose for the greenhouse.
how: One person can sit on the grass, off center, looking at the trees.
They stay small. The lawn and the greenhouse are the frame.
One frame.

shots.stand: South side of the deck. The city fills the lower two thirds.
shots.angle: On the South observatory, at the south glass. The city fills the lower two thirds. The deck edge can be a line at the bottom so the height reads.
shots.light: You are here from 16:20. Sunset is 17:06. Take one while the sun is still on the towers, and one after the lights are on, before 18:15. If Fuji is out, it sits past the towers on the southwest.
how: Hold the camera against the glass if the reflection of the room is in the picture, or step to an open section.
Keep the horizon level.
Two frames, then the neon walk.

shots.stand: At the entrance of an alley that does not forbid photos. Lanterns overhead. The lane a slot.
shots.angle: Stand at the mouth. The lanterns stack. The lane narrows. Doors are the walls.
shots.light: Night. The lanterns are the light. No flash.
how: If a sign says no photos, use the next alley.
Do not shoot into a bar.
One frame, then walk in.

shots.stand: A few doors in, full length, a lantern beside them.
shots.angle: You stay at the entrance. One person stands a few doors in, off to the side so people can pass. A lantern is beside them, not behind the head.
shots.light: Night. No flash. The nearest lantern lights the coat.
how: They look down the alley.
They do not block a door.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the glass platform, face down, the crossing directly below.
shots.angle: Sky Edge is the glass corner that looks down on the scramble. Lie flat. The crossing fills the frame as stripes and people. Include the glass edge so the drop is in the picture.
shots.light: Your slot is morning, about 10:00. The sun is high. The stripes are the bright part. Expose for the crossing.
how: There is a short queue. Staff will place you.
Both hands on the camera, pointed straight down.
One frame of the crossing full, then one as it clears.

shots.stand: At the west edge, the skyline in front of you.
shots.angle: Stand at the western rail. The city fills the lower two thirds. On a clear morning Fuji can sit on the southwest horizon, small.
shots.light: 10:00. This deck is famous at sunset. In the morning the picture is the city in daylight, not the orange sky.
how: Hold the camera level.
A person at the rail, back to you, can stand at the edge of the frame.
One frame, then the shops.

shots.look: Person in front of the crossing
shots.stand: From the far corner. They walk toward you. The signs are behind them.
shots.angle: Street level, on a corner across the crossing. One person from your group walks toward you, full length, as the light changes. The signs and the buildings are the background. The stripes are under them.
shots.light: Morning side light. Expose for them. The brightest screen can blow out.
how: They keep walking with the crowd.
You stay on the sidewalk.
One frame, then step back.

shots.look: The crossing from the Tsutaya window
shots.stand: Second floor of Shibuya Tsutaya, through the Starbucks glass, looking down.
shots.angle: From the window that faces the crossing. The intersection is the subject. Heads along the bottom are fine. The signs wrap the top.
shots.light: Daylight. The signs are already on. Expose for the street.
how: The window seats fill up. Take it when you can see the stripes.
Shoot through the glass, camera close to it so the room reflection drops out.
One frame as the crowd steps off.

shots.stand: Ginza 4-chome corner, the clock tower filling the top.
shots.angle: From the corner at Ginza 4-chome. The Wako clock tower fills the top. Chuo-dori goes back. Friday the street has cars, so you stay on the corner.
shots.light: Late afternoon on the way to Tokyo Tower. The stone is warm. If the lights are on, take a second frame.
how: Keep the clock in the frame.
The crossing can be in the lower third.
One frame, then keep moving. Tower is 16:20.

shots.stand: One window, the display filling the frame.
shots.angle: At one window, Itoya or a lit front. The display fills the frame. Your reflection stays out of the glass.
shots.light: Late day, or the window light once the shops turn their lamps on.
how: Step sideways until the street reflection leaves the display.
One object, or one wall of paper, filling the frame.
One frame.

shots.stand: Plaza in front of the gate. They stand in the opening. The tower rises beside the roof.
shots.angle: From the plaza, far enough back that the tower tip and their whole body both fit. They stand in the gate opening. The tower sits just clear of the roof.
shots.light: You are here around 18:25. The tower is lit orange. The gate is still readable. Expose for them.
how: They stand full length in the opening.
Step back until the tip is in.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the park path, trees in the foreground, the tower centered.
shots.angle: In Shiba Park, on the path where the tower sits between the trees. The trunks frame it. The tower is large, not a pin above the leaves.
shots.light: Dusk, on the walk from the tower to the gate. The lattice is orange against a deep sky.
how: Walk until a gap in the trees puts the tower in the middle.
Keep it vertical.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the Mori plaza, the tower through Maman's legs.
shots.angle: On the Roppongi Hills plaza. Stand so one of the spider's legs frames the shot and Mori Tower sits in the gap. If you are on the other side of the complex, the tower alone, filling the frame from the plaza.
shots.light: After 21:00. The tower is a grid of lights. Expose for the lights. The plaza can go dark.
how: Crouch or stand so the legs make a frame, not a blur across the lens.
Keep the tower vertical.
One frame.

shots.stand: At the summit lookout, Fuji beyond the ridge if the sky is clear.
shots.angle: From the summit lookout. The ridge and the trees are the foreground. Fuji, when it is out, sits in the distance, small and sharp.
shots.light: Daytime, after the climb. Clear air is the whole game. Haze hides the mountain even on a blue day.
how: If Fuji is out, put it on a third, with the ridge under it.
People at the rail stay at the edge.
One frame, then the walk down. The onsen is the stop, not another viewpoint.

shots.stand: From the steps, the hall or the tengu straight on.
shots.angle: From the steps in front of the hall, or in front of a tengu. The statue or the hall fills the frame. The forest is the side.
shots.light: Forest shade. Even light. No hard sun on the face of the statue if you can step into the shade.
how: Hold the camera straight.
Leave the worship space clear.
One frame.

shots.look: Pagoda and Fuji from the deck
shots.stand: Do not stop at the pagoda. Walk up the path behind it to the observation deck.
shots.angle: From the deck above the pagoda. The pagoda is in the foreground, Fuji is behind it, and the town sits between them.
shots.light: Around 09:10, if the morning is clear. October has no blossom. Early autumn color may be on the trees. The alignment is the same without it.
how: Set the frame before you step onto the crowded rail.
Hold the camera level. Spire and summit both in.
One frame. If Fuji is in cloud, the lake later is the place to wait.

shots.stand: At the end of the rail, full length, pagoda and Fuji in front of them.
shots.angle: From just behind them on the deck. One person stands at the rail, looking out. The pagoda and Fuji stay in the frame past them.
shots.light: Morning. Expose for them. The mountain can be brighter.
how: They look at the view.
You stay off the middle of the rail.
One frame, then start down. The bus time depends on leaving the pagoda.

shots.stand: At Arakura Fuji Sengen, on the way up, the torii framing the mountain.
shots.angle: On the shrine approach, before the long stairs. Stand so Fuji sits in the opening of the red torii.
shots.light: Morning, only if the summit is clear of cloud.
how: One frame on the way up.
Then the stairs. The deck behind the pagoda is the main frame.

shots.stand: Southwest corner of the moat. The stone bridge, the pine, the watchtower.
shots.angle: From the southwest corner of the moat. The stone bridge leads in. The pine sits in front of the iron bridge. The Fushimi watchtower is behind.
shots.light: The run is 06:00. Sunrise is just before that. The bridge is in the first light and the water is still.
how: Stop once. Keep the horizon level.
A runner on the path can stay at the edge.
One frame, then finish the loop.

shots.stand: Full length, signs stacked behind them.
shots.angle: On the main street, near Radio Kaikan. One person stands full length. A vertical stack of signs is the background. They are sharp.
shots.light: Late morning, in the shade between the buildings, so the face is even.
how: They look just off camera, weight on one leg.
You stay out of the frame.
One frame, then off the curb.

shots.stand: In the street, camera pointed up, signs filling the frame.
shots.angle: Stand on the sidewalk and point up. The signs stack and there is no horizon.
shots.light: Sunday daytime. The signs are already on. Expose for them.
how: A vertical frame.
Keep the camera from tilting so the buildings lean.
One frame.

shots.stand: Across the aisle at Mandarake. Figures above, shelves below.
shots.angle: Stand across the aisle so the whole front fits. The hanging figures fill the top. The shelves fill the bottom. A person browsing can stand at the far edge.
shots.light: Indoor shop light. The windows can blow out.
how: Include one figure and the books under it.
Focus on the figure.
One frame.

shots.stand: One piece, large, the forest behind it, a strip of sky.
shots.angle: Pick one work and walk until it is large in the frame. The forest is the background. The sky is a strip. The tower you can walk inside is the obvious one. A single figure on the grass uses the same setup.
shots.light: Morning, between 09:05 and noon. Side light. Walk around the piece until the light is on the face you want.
how: One piece per frame.
People stay out, or at the base, small.
Leave the lawn by 12:00 so the boat still runs.

shots.stand: At the rail, the valley and the steam filling the frame.
shots.angle: At the viewing rail. The valley fills the frame and the steam rises through it. A person at the rail can be small, at the edge.
shots.light: Midday, flat and bright. The steam is the subject. Expose so the steam stays white and the rock stays dark.
how: Stay on the safe side of the barrier.
One frame.
The smell is strong. Take it and step back.

shots.stand: One car against the mountain, or the valley through the window.
shots.angle: From the platform, one car against the slope. On the ride, the camera goes against the glass so the valley is the picture and your reflection is not.
shots.light: Open daylight. The mountain is the exposure.
how: On the platform, one frame of the car.
In the car, one frame through the glass, camera touching it.
Then Owakudani. The ground stop is 45–60 minutes.

shots.stand: On the stone platform in front of the torii, the lake framed in the opening.
shots.angle: This is the frame the line is for. Stand on the platform facing the gate. One person stands in the opening, full length. The red posts frame them. The lake is behind the gate.
shots.light: Afternoon sun on the red. If they are in shade and the gate is in sun, wait until both match.
how: The line moves. Have the frame ready before it is your turn.
They look at the lake, or just off camera.
One frame, then leave the platform for the next person.

shots.stand: Lake side of the boat, gate against the trees.
shots.angle: On the side facing the shrine, as the boat nears Moto-Hakone. The gate is smaller than it will be from the shore. The forest is the backdrop. Water fills the lower half.
shots.light: Afternoon. October color on the hill is enough.
how: Take it at the closest pass.
Keep the mountain in.
The shore platform is the close frame.

shots.look: Gate and Fuji from the port
shots.stand: South end of the Moto-Hakone port walkway, about 500 m from the gate.
shots.angle: This is a different spot from the platform. The gate faces the bay, and Fuji is behind the shrine hill, so you cannot get both from the jetty. From the port walkway the gate sits under Fuji.
shots.light: Only if Fuji is clear. Afternoon haze often hides it.
how: If the summit is out, one frame, gate low, Fuji above it.
If it is in cloud, skip this and stay at the shrine.
The bus wants you off the lake by 16:10.

shots.stand: Middle of the lane, signs as the ceiling, stalls going back.
shots.angle: Stand in the middle of the arcade. The lane recedes. The hanging signs make the ceiling. Stalls are both walls.
shots.light: 16:15 onward. The ends of the arcade are in late daylight. The stalls are lit.
how: Eye level.
Wait for a gap.
One frame. The stalls are closing, so this is a short stop.

shots.stand: Pickles, knives, or tamago, filling the frame.
shots.angle: At one stall. The food or the knives fill the frame. The stall lamp is the light.
shots.light: Under the arcade, the bulb on the goods. The aisle behind can fall off.
how: Close. One pile, or one row of knives.
Hands in the frame only if they are yours or the seller is fine with it.
One frame.

shots.stand: On Shirakawa, at Tatsumi bridge. Water in the lower third, willows and a lantern.
shots.angle: From the bridge or the canal path just beside it. The teahouses and lattice are across the water. One lantern reflects.
shots.light: From 17:30. Sunset is about then, and the lanterns are coming on. Expose for the lantern.
how: This is the Gion frame. Hanamikoji is the street. Shirakawa is the picture.
Keep the horizon level.
One frame.

shots.stand: Full length on the Shirakawa path, a lantern beside them.
shots.angle: On the path. One person, full length. A lantern is beside them, not directly behind the head. The canal is in the frame.
shots.light: Dusk. The lantern is warmer than the sky. Expose for their face.
how: They look along the canal.
This is your group. Leave anyone in maiko dress to walk.
Do not pose in front of a private doorway.

shots.stand: In a public lane, from the chest up.
shots.angle: Close. Face and collar. They look just past the lens. The lane behind them is dark and soft.
shots.light: Open shade, or the last daylight.
how: This is someone from your group.
Shoulders turned, eyes just off camera.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the path, camera tilted up, trunks on both sides, leaves closing overhead.
shots.angle: Stand in the middle of the path and point up it. The stalks are the walls. The canopy is the ceiling. A strip of path stays at the bottom.
shots.light: From 07:15. Light on the upper leaves, the path in shade. This is the hour it is empty.
how: A wide frame.
Wait until the path ahead is clear.
One frame. Out by 07:40.

shots.stand: Center of the path, full length, a solid-color coat.
shots.angle: You stand further down the path. One person stands in the center, full length, looking up the path. The bamboo is the wall on both sides.
shots.light: Morning light on the tops of the stalks, and enough on them that they are not a silhouette.
how: Red, black, or white.
They look up the path.
Only while it is empty.

shots.stand: Seated on the main hall veranda. Pond below, Arashiyama hill behind. That hill is the picture.
shots.angle: Sit on the veranda. The pond fills the lower half. The far shore and the hill are centered the way the garden is built. Do not start from the side path.
shots.light: From 08:30. Soft morning. The water is still. Expose for the hill and the far trees.
how: Sit, so the veranda edge is a line at the bottom.
The middle of the pond stays clear.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the east path under the stage, the wooden platform out over the trees.
shots.angle: From the path below the stage, on the east side. The pillars and the deck stick out over the hillside. The whole structure fits, including the drop under it.
shots.light: 08:00. Morning sun on the wood.
how: Step back until the stage and the trees under it are both in.
People on the deck can be small.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the stage, at the rail, looking out. You are behind them.
shots.angle: On the deck. One or two people stand at the rail, full length, looking at the trees. You stand behind them so their backs and the view are both in the frame.
shots.light: 08:00, before the deck fills. Expose for them. The view is brighter.
how: They look out.
Include their feet and the rail.
One frame.

shots.look: People in front of the gate
shots.stand: A loose group, full length, the gate and the pagoda behind.
shots.angle: In the plaza by the gate. Full length, a step of space between people. The gate roof and the three-story pagoda stay behind them.
shots.light: Morning on them and on the red gate.
how: They can look at you. Shoulders turned a little.
Step back until the roof is in.
One frame, then off the steps.

shots.stand: On the lane south of Yasaka pagoda, looking up. The tower sits between the eaves.
shots.angle: Yasaka-dori, south of the pagoda, looking north. The five roofs are centered. The wooden shopfronts make the sides.
shots.light: Around 10:00, walking down from Kiyomizu. Late morning sun on the pagoda. The lane is busy. The frame needs a gap.
how: Wait for a gap in the middle.
Keep the spire in.
One frame.

shots.stand: On Sannenzaka, looking down the slope, the stone and the shop eaves leading the eye.
shots.angle: Partway down the slope. The paving runs away from you. The wooden fronts and noren are the sides. A person from your group can be in the lower part of the frame, walking.
shots.light: Late morning.
how: Step out of the walking line.
One frame when the middle of the slope is open.
The pagoda frame is the other street, south of the tower.

shots.stand: From below them. Two people, full length, the pagoda or the eaves behind.
shots.angle: From lower on the lane. Two people walk up, full length. The pagoda or the shop eaves stay behind them.
shots.light: Late morning. Expose for them.
how: They look ahead.
You stay below, off the walking line.
One frame.

shots.stand: A few minutes up from the main gate, inside the tunnel, against one row.
shots.angle: Stand against one row of gates. The near pillars are sharp, the writing readable. The path curves away. A lantern sits further down.
shots.light: From 07:00. Side light between the gates. This lower tunnel fills after 07:30.
how: Shoot along the row.
Wait until the middle of the path is clear.
One frame, then keep climbing. The upper gates are the empty ones.

shots.stand: Past the first tunnel, where the path is quiet.
shots.angle: Further up the mountain. One corridor of gates, the near gate large, the rest stacking into the trees.
shots.light: Still morning. Fewer people than the lower tunnel. The light rakes across one side of the red.
how: Pick a bend where one side is lit.
The path in the middle stays clear.
One frame. The train to Nara is 10:15.

shots.stand: Close, from behind, against the gates, off the walking line.
shots.angle: From behind, close. They stand beside the tunnel, against the gates. A patterned kimono or a deep-colored coat is the subject. The gates are the wall.
shots.light: Morning side light on the cloth.
how: They face the gates.
A pale coat disappears against the red.
Focus on the shoulders. One frame.

shots.stand: On the grass near Kōfuku-ji, the pagoda behind the deer.
shots.angle: On the lawn by Kōfuku-ji, which is on the walk in from the station. A few deer on the grass. The five-story pagoda is behind them, complete.
shots.light: Around 11:00. The light is harder than early morning. Expose for the deer. The pagoda can be bright.
how: Take it before the crackers come out.
Keep the pagoda roof in.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the grass. Full length, one arm out, one deer in the center.
shots.angle: The person stands to one side, full length, one arm extended. One deer reaches up. Trees or a roof sit behind.
shots.light: Late morning sun from the side, on the person and the deer together.
how: They look at the deer.
The cracker stays in the hand.
Focus on the hand and the deer's head. One frame.

shots.stand: Straight on, the great gate filling the frame.
shots.angle: From the approach, straight on. The gate fills the frame. Both guardians are in it if you are close enough to see them under the roof. The roof is complete.
shots.light: Midday. The sun is hard. The shadow under the gate is part of the picture. Expose for the wood under the eaves.
how: Hold the camera straight.
Stand on the center line, then step aside if a group is in the opening.
One frame.

shots.stand: Inside, from the front, the face and the halo.
shots.angle: Inside the hall, from the front. A vertical frame. The face and the halo fill it.
shots.light: The hall is dark and the face is lit from the front opening. Expose for the face. No flash.
how: Brace against a post or use both hands. The hall is dim.
Keep the face sharp.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the approach. One lantern large in front. Deer on the path if they are there.
shots.angle: The nearest stone lantern is sharp and large. The row behind it steps into the cedars. A deer on the path, between the lanterns, is the frame people come for at this hour.
shots.light: 15:00. Low sun through the cedars onto the stone.
how: Get close to the front lantern.
Focus on the lantern, or on the deer if one is standing in the row.
One frame. The train is 16:30.

shots.stand: At one stall, steam and the food filling the frame.
shots.angle: At one grill. Steam, the food, and the cook's hands fill the frame. The rest of the market stays out.
shots.light: Under the arcade, 12:15 to 13:45. The stall light on the food. Midday in the street is harsh, so stay under the roof.
how: Close.
Focus on the food, with the steam in front of it.
One frame while the grills are still open.

shots.stand: In the aisle, stalls on both sides, the lane going back.
shots.angle: Stand in the aisle. Stalls on both sides. The lane recedes. A stall sign can sit at the top.
shots.light: Mixed daylight and stall bulbs. Expose for the stalls.
how: Eye level.
A gap in the aisle.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the Tombori walk at the water, not only from the bridge. The signs reflect in the canal.
shots.angle: At water level on the river walk. The Glico runner and the stack of signs are across the canal. The water fills the lower third and carries the color.
shots.light: After full dark. Mid-October that is after about 17:30. Expose for the signs.
how: The runner is the billboard.
Include the reflection.
One frame. No flash.

shots.stand: On the bridge, full length, the signs behind them.
shots.angle: On Ebisubashi. One person, full length. A sign is readable behind them. They are sharp.
shots.light: After the lights are on. Expose for them. The signs can run hot.
how: They look along the canal.
You stand a few steps away.
One frame.

shots.stand: Two minutes south of the neon. The stone alley, paper lanterns, the mossy statue at the end.
shots.angle: At the mouth of Hozenji Yokocho. The lane is narrow. Lanterns overhead. The moss-covered Fudo is at the end, small, in the middle.
shots.light: Night. The lanterns are the light. No flash.
how: One frame down the lane.
If people are at the statue, leave them to it.
Then back to the canal.

shots.look: Tsutenkaku at the end of the street
shots.stand: In the shopping street, the tower centered at the end, signs around its base.
shots.angle: Stand in the street so the tower sits at the end of it. The shop signs lead to it. The billboards at its feet stay in the frame.
shots.light: Morning, 09:30 onward. The tower against a pale sky. The blue-hour version of this frame is after sunset, which is not this morning's window.
how: Walk until the tower is large.
Keep it vertical.
One frame.

shots.stand: In the covered market, one kushikatsu sign filling the frame.
shots.angle: Inside the alley. One sign is large. The lane recedes behind it. The roof is the top of the frame.
shots.light: Morning shade under the roof, stall lights on.
how: Close to one sign.
One frame.

shots.stand: On the bridge at the moat. The stone walls lead in. The tower is large.
shots.angle: From Gokurakubashi. The bridge and the walls make the lines. The tower sits at the end of them, large. Water in the lower third.
shots.light: Afternoon side light on the white walls.
how: If the tower is small, you are on the wrong side of the park. Walk to this bridge.
Keep the horizon level.
One frame.
